title: Understanding Squared Loss
text: Squared loss is a way to measure how far off our predictions are from the actual values. It involves squaring the difference between each predicted probability and the true label. Can you identify the differences for each pair?

title: Calculating Differences
text: For each true label and predicted probability pair, calculate the difference. For example, if the true label is $$0$$ and the predicted probability is $$0.1$$, the difference is $$0-0.1$$. What are the differences for the other pairs?

title: Squaring the Differences
text: Once you have the differences, square each one. Remember, squaring a negative number results in a positive value. What are the squared values for each pair?

title: Choosing the Correct Squared Loss
text: Select the expression that represents the total squared loss for the given true labels and predicted probabilities.
